title: Standardize overload error payload + headers (Retry-After) for Hosted endpoints + OpenAI-compat mapping
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
## Context
As part of the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding initiative, we need stable customer-facing overload behavior. Today under burst traffic customers see a mix of 500/502/503/timeouts across gateway/routing/runtime, which encourages aggressive retries and causes retry storms.

This ticket defines and implements a *single* standardized overload error shape + headers across:
- Redwood REST endpoints (native)
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings)

Primary requirements:
1) Consistent HTTP status codes for overload-protected failures (prefer 429 or 503 depending on condition).
2) Always include `Retry-After` when the client can retry.
3) Include Redwood-specific error codes to make client + support action deterministic.
4) Avoid breaking existing OpenAI-compatible client expectations.

## Goals
- Make overload errors deterministic, cacheable, and customer-actionable.
- Ensure the gateway and routing/runtime can propagate a shared error code/reason end-to-end.
- Provide explicit retry guidance (header + message semantics) and discourage tight loops.

## Non-goals
- Replacing existing quota/rate limiting semantics (those remain separate).
- Introducing customer-specific bespoke error payloads.

## Proposed behavior (summary)
### Headers
For overload-protected responses:
- `Retry-After: <seconds>` (integer seconds). Present when retry is appropriate.
- `X-Redwood-Error-Code: <CODE>` (stable machine code; see below).
- `X-Redwood-Overload-Reason: <REASON>` (optional; lower cardinality string; not per-tenant).
- Ensure we still include existing request correlation header(s): `X-Request-Id` / `X-Redwood-Request-Id` (whichever is current standard).

### HTTP status mapping
- `429 Too Many Requests`:
  - Admission control / tier-based shedding at the edge when capacity is available but we are protecting fairness / preventing queue blowups.
  - Default when the platform expects quick recovery and wants clients to back off.
- `503 Service Unavailable`:
  - Region/model pool saturation or downstream runtime protection where service is temporarily unable to serve.
  - Used when gateway/routing believes capacity is constrained and/or fallback was not possible.

### Error payload (Redwood native)
JSON response:
- `error.type`: `"overload"`
- `error.code`: stable Redwood code (see list)
- `error.message`: short human-friendly summary (no internal details)
- `error.request_id`: request id string
- `error.retry_after_seconds`: integer (mirrors Retry-After when present)

### Error payload (OpenAI-compat)
Must conform to typical OpenAI client parsing:
- Root: `{ "error": { "message": "...", "type": "server_error"|"rate_limit_error", "code": "..." } }`
- `type` mapping:
  - 429 => `rate_limit_error` (even though it’s overload, this matches client behavior expectations)
  - 503 => `server_error`
- `code` uses Redwood stable error codes (string) to preserve machine-actionability.
- Include `Retry-After` header in all cases where retry is appropriate.

## Stable Redwood overload error codes (v1)
These should be used across gateway/routing/runtime, but this ticket focuses on the customer-facing mapping + schema:
- `OVERLOAD_ADMISSION_REJECTED` (edge admission control / fairness)
- `OVERLOAD_BREAKER_OPEN` (routing breaker state open)
- `OVERLOAD_QUEUE_FULL` (bounded queue exceeded)
- `OVERLOAD_RUNTIME_BACKPRESSURE` (shed at runtime scheduling boundary)
- `OVERLOAD_MEMORY_PRESSURE` (KV-cache / memory guardrail)
- `OVERLOAD_DEPENDENCY_TIMEOUT` (explicitly classified downstream timeout that is overload-protected; do **not** use for generic timeouts)

Notes:
- Keep the code set small; avoid per-model or per-route codes.
- Messages must not include customer identifiers or internal cluster names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] For all hosted endpoints that can shed, overload-protected failures return a standardized payload + headers.
- [x] `Retry-After` is set on 429/503 where retry is safe; absent where retry is not recommended.
- [x] OpenAI-compat endpoints return an error object compatible with common SDK parsers; `code` is present and stable.
- [x] Unit tests cover:
  - status code mapping
  - header presence / formatting
  - payload schema conformance
  - OpenAI-compat mapping
- [x] Confirm with SRE/PM what is considered “overload-protected” for SLO accounting (see ADR).

## References
- ADR: adr-0147-overload-error-taxonomy-and-http-mapping.json
- Initiative: ENG-4821
- Gateway admission hook: ENG-4822
- SDK surfacing follow-up: ENG-4836

## Implementation notes
- Prefer a shared library/module for error serialization + code enum to avoid drift between REST and OpenAI-compat.
- `Retry-After` should be sourced from breaker cooldown / routing hint when available; otherwise use conservative defaults (e.g., 1–5s for admission, 10–30s for breaker open) and tune post-canary.
- Ensure we don’t accidentally classify “auth failure / invalid request” as overload.
- Ensure `Retry-After` is integer seconds (not HTTP date) to reduce client parsing mistakes.
comments: 2025-10-16 - Rafael Mendes: Creating as P0. Customer escalations (SUP-3928, SUP-3961) are explicitly asking for consistent errors + retry guidance. Please align with ADR-0147 and keep OpenAI-compat behavior conservative.

2025-10-21 - Brian Murphy: Drafted v1 error code list and OpenAI-compat mapping. Key question: do we use 429 for breaker-open? Proposal: breaker-open => 503 (capacity constrained) unless explicitly edge-admission fairness. Will sync with SRE/PM.

2025-10-23 - Henry Cho: +1 to 503 for breaker-open. Messaging should avoid implying “you are rate limited”; but accept that OpenAI clients use `rate_limit_error` for 429 and behave well (exponential backoff). For 503 use `server_error`.

2025-10-24 - Christine Wong: Please make sure `Retry-After` is always set when breaker-open. We’ve seen clients hammer when they get ambiguous 503/timeouts. Also ensure the code is plumbed through logs/traces for incident correlation.

2025-10-28 - Brian Murphy: Implementation started as shared `OverloadError` serializer used by both `/v1/*` and OpenAI-compat handlers. Added `X-Redwood-Error-Code` and `Retry-After`. Need follow-up from gateway/routing to pass through reason fields consistently.
2025-11-02 - Mina Haddad: Routing can provide `retry_after_seconds` from breaker cooldown. Please ensure header respects routing-provided value and doesn’t overwrite with defaults.

2025-11-08 - Brian Murphy: Added tests for OpenAI-compat mapping in `redwood-openai-compat`. Noted edge case: streaming disconnects must still emit an initial headers frame with `Retry-After` when we reject before streaming starts; once streaming started we can only terminate the stream with a structured terminal message (handled in ENG-4822/Runtime tickets).

2025-11-18 - Nikhil Sharma: Product approval for error code naming: keep `OVERLOAD_*` prefix, avoid exposing internal component names. Also confirm billing: overload-protected failures are not billed; make sure message doesn’t mention billing but remains consistent with docs/FAQ.

2025-12-04 - Brian Murphy: PRs up: shared enum + schema, plus OpenAI-compat mapping. Waiting on final review from SRE for header names + defaults. After merge, SDK tickets (ENG-4836) can start consuming the codes.

2026-01-09 - Rafael Mendes: Canary feedback: `Retry-After` defaults were too low for breaker-open; clients still retried aggressively and stayed in hot loop. Please adjust defaults to align with observed recovery time and routing cooldown.

2026-01-12 - Brian Murphy: Updated: breaker-open default `Retry-After` 20s when routing doesn’t supply; admission rejected default 2s. Added guard: clamp 1s–60s. Re-ran contract tests against OpenAI client libraries (python/ts) in CI.
2026-01-17 - Brian Murphy: Merged and deployed behind feature flag. Marking Done. Follow-ups: docs wording (ENG-4832) and SDK surfacing (ENG-4836).
